category_title: Students requiring structured accountability during phonics dictation
scenario_title: Phonics dictation and spelling pattern transfer
minimal_context: The student is spelling and reading a list of words with the 'ook' pattern during a phonics dictation routine.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please write down the word 'cook' on your paper.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Yes. Now I want you to sit quietly and read that list of words by yourself over and over until time is up.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Slides out of his chair and begins rolling on the floor instead of reading the list individually)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Please write down the word 'cook' on your paper.

STUDENT: c - o - o - k

TUTOR: Okay. Now write down 'look', 'hook', and 'took'.

STUDENT: It's the ook family.

TUTOR: Yes. Now I want you to sit quietly and read that list of words by yourself over and over until time is up.

STUDENT: (Slides out of his chair and begins rolling on the floor instead of reading the list individually)

task.content: Spelling words using the 'ook' spelling pattern (e.g., 'cook') and making choices between 'c' and 'k', then transferring the pattern to other words
task.learning_goal: Shift from the less rigorous literacy practices of early childhood to being able to focus on literacy instruction in a full-day, school setting

context.social_setting: Whole class, working individually and with a neighbor
context.time_context: During a dictation routine and blending routine

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When curriculum activities are overly repetitive or solitary

behavior_patterns.condition: When asked to share their spelling attempt
When practicing with several words using the same spelling pattern
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Pointed out confidently the linguistic pattern
